G4600.def:
σιαγών, -όνος, ἡ 
[in LXX for לְחִי ;] 
the jawbone, jaw, cheek: Matthieu 5:39, Luc 6:29 (cf. MM, xxii).†

G4601.def:
σιγάω, -ῶ
(σιγή), [in LXX for חָרַשׁ, חָשָׁה, etc. ;] 
__1. intrans., to be silent, keep silence: Luc 9:36 18:39 20:26, Actes 12:17 15:12-13, 1 Corinthiens 14:28 14:30 14:34. 
__2. Trans., to keep secret; pass., to be kept secret: Romains 16:25.†
SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιωπάω

G4602.def:
σιγή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX: Wis.18:14, 3Ma.3:23 * ;] 
silence: Actes 21:40, Apocalypse 8:1.†

G4603.def:
σιδήρεος, -α, -ον (-οῦς, -ᾶ -οῦν)
(σίδηρος), [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;] 
of iron: Actes 12:10, Apocalypse 2:27 9:9 12:5 19:15.†

G4604.def:
σίδηρος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;] 
iron: Apocalypse 18:12.†

G4605.def:
Σιδών, -ῶnος, ἡ (Heb. צִידוֹן), 
Sidon, a maritime city of Phœnicia: Matthieu 11:21-22 15:21, Marc 3:8 7:24, 31, Luc 6:17 10:13-14, Actes 27:3.†

G4607.def:
σικάριος, -ου, ὁ
(Lat.; sica, a dagger carried under their clothing by the Sicarii), 
a bandit, assassin, one of the Sicarii (FlJ, B.J., ii, 17, 6, al.): Actes 21:38.†

G4608.def:
σίκερα, τό indecl. 
(Aram. שִׁכְרָא), [in LXX for שֵׁכָר (also rendered μέθυσμα, Juges 13:4, Michée 2:11), Lévitique 10:9, al. ;] 
fermented liquor, strong drink: Luc 1:15.†

G4609.def:
Σίλας, -α (accusative to BL, § 29, W-Schm., 74, -ᾶς, -ᾶ), ὁ (Aram. שׁאִילָא; see Dalman, Gr., 157.5), 
Silas (called also Σιλουανός, which see): Actes 15:22, 27 15:32, 34 15:40 16:19, 25 16:29 17:4, 10 17:14-15 18:5 †

G4610.def:
Σιλουανός
(in MSS also Σιλβανός, a form frequently in π.), -οῦ, ὁ, 
Silvanus, latinized name of Silas: 2 Corinthiens 1:19, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:1, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:1, 1 Pierre 5:12.†

G4611.def:
Σιλωάμ (indecl., but in FlJ, genitive, ᾶ, B.J., ii, 16, 2), ὁ (Heb. שִׁלֹחַ), 
Siloam (see DB, iii, 515 f.): Luc 13:4, Jean 9:7, 11.†

G4612.def:
σιμικίνθιον (also written σημι-), -ου, τό (Lat. semicinctium), 
a work­man's apron: Actes 19:12.†

G4613G.def:
Σίμων, -ωνος, ὁ 
a Greek name (transliterated סִימוֺן in Heb.) used as a substitute for Συμεών (which see), Simon 
__1. Simon Peter: Matthieu 17:25, Marc 1:29, al. 
__2. Simon the Zealot (see: ζηλωτής, Καναναῖος): Matthieu 10:4, Marc 3:18, Luc 6:15, Actes 1:13. 
__3. One of the Brethren of our Lord (see: ἀδελψός): Matthieu 13:55, Marc 6:3. 
__4. The father of Judas Iscariot, himself surnamed Ἰσκαριώτης (which see): Jean 6:71 12:4 (Rec.) 13:2,26 
__5. Simon the Cyrenian: Matthieu 27:32, Marc 15:21, Luc 23:26. 
__6. Simon the Pharisee: Luc 7:40, 43-44. 
__7. Simon of Bethany, surnamed ὁ λεπρός: Matthieu 26:6, Marc 14:3. 
__8. Simon Magus, a Samaritan sorcerer: Actes 8:9, 13 8:18, 24. 
__9. Simon the tanner, of Joppa: Actes 9:43 10:6, 17 10:32

Σίμων, -ωνος, ὁ

__2. Simon the Zealot (see: ζηλωτής, Καναναῖος): Matthieu 10:4, Marc 3:18, Luc 6:15, Actes 1:13.

__8. Simon Magus, a Samaritan sorcerer: Actes 8:9, 13 8:18, 24. 
__9. Simon the tanner, of Joppa: Actes 9:43 10:6, 17 10:32

G4614.def:
Σινά
(-ᾶ, Rec.), 
indecl. (but τὸ Σιναῖον, FlJ, Ant., iii, 5, 1; τὸ Σιναῖον ὄρος, ib. ii, 12, 1), τό 
(Heb. סִינַי), 
Sinai (Exode 19:11, al.): Actes 7:30, 38, Galates 4:24-25†

G4615.def:
σίναπι, -εως, τό
(prob. Egyptian), = Attic τὸ νᾶπυ 
mustard: Matthieu 13:31 17:20, Marc 4:31, Luc 13:19 17:6.†

G4617.def:
σινιάω
(σίνιον, a sieve), = σήθω, 
to sift, winnow: figuratively, Luc 22:31.†

G4618.def:
σιτευτός, -ή, -όν
(σιτεύω, to feed, fatten), [in LXX: 3Ki.4:23 (אָבַס), etc. ;] 
fattened: Luc 15:23, 27 15:30.†

G4619.def:
σιτιστός, -ή, -όν
(σιτίζω, to fatten) [in Sm.: Psaumes 22:13, Jérémie 46:21 * ;] 
= σιτευτός, fattened; as subst., pl., τὰ σ., fatlings: Matthieu 22:4.†

G4620.def:
σιτομέτριον, -ου, τό
(σιτομετρέω, Genèse 47:12, 14 *, = Attic τὸν σῖτον μετρέω), 
a measured portion of food: Luc 12:42 (for exx. in π., see Deiss., BS, 158; LAE, 103.1).†

G4621.def:
σῖτος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for דָּגָן ;] 
wheat, corn: Matthieu 3:12 13:25, 29-30 Marc 4:28, Luc 3:17 12:18 16:7 22:32, Jean 12:24, Actes 27:38, 1 Corinthiens 15:37, Apocalypse 6:6 18:13.†
σιτίοι, -ου, τό 
(dimin. of σῖτος), [in LXX: Proverbes 30:22 (לֶחֶם)* ;] 
__1. corn, grain: Actes 7:12 (but see 131., § 9, 1). 
__2. Mostly in pl., σιτία, bread, food, provisions (LXX, l.with, Hdt., al.).†

G4623.def:
σιωπάω, -ῶ
(σιωπή, silence) [in LXX for חָשָׁה, חָרַשׁ hi., etc. ;] 
to be silent or still, keep silence: Matthieu 20:31 26:63, Marc 3:4 9:34 10:48 14:61, Luc 19:4, Actes 18:9; of one dumb, Luc 1:20 (cf. 4Ma.10:18); addressed rhetorically to the sea, σιώπα, Marc 4:39.†
SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιγάω (which see)

G4624.def:
σκανδαλίζω
(σκάνδαλον), [in LXX: Dan LXX 11:41 (כָּשַׁל ni.), Sir.9:5 (Sir.35:15 32:15) (יָקֹשׁ ho.) Sir.23:8 (also in Aq., Sm., Th., and in Psa Sol Psaumes 16:7; not elsewhere, except NT and eccl.)* ;] 
prop., to put a snare or stumbling-block in the way; in NT always metaphorically of that which hinders right conduct or thought, to cause to stumble: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 5:29-30 17:27 18:6, 8-9 Marc 9:42-43, 45 9:47 Luc 17:2, Jean 6:61, 1 Corinthiens 8:13. Pass., to be made to stumble, to stumble: Matthieu 11:6 13:21, 57 15:12 24:10 26:31, 33, Marc 4:17 6:3 14:27, 29, Luc 7:23, Jean 16:1, Romains 14:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), 2 Corinthiens 11:29,†

G4626.def:
σκάπτω 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 5:6 (עֲדַר ni.)* ;] 
to dig: Luc 6:48 13:8 16:3.†

G4627.def:
σκάφη, -ης, ἡ
(σκάπτω), [in LXX: Dan LXX Bel 1:32, TH Bel 1:33 * ;] 
anything scooped out, esp. a light boat, skiff: Actes 27:16, 30 27:32.†

G4628.def:
σκέλος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX for רֶגֶל, etc. ;] 
the leg from the hip downwards: ?Jean 19:3-33 †

G4629.def:
σκέπασμα, -τος, τό
(σκεπάζω, to cover), 
a covering, esp. clothing: 1 Timothée 6:8.†

G4631.def:
σκευή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX: 3Ma.5:45 R * ;] 
equipment, tackle: Actes 27:19.†

G4632.def:
σκεῦος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי ;] 
a vessel, implement (for exx. in various senses, see MM, xxii): Marc 11:16, Luc 8:16, Jean 19:29, Actes 10:11, 16 11:5, Romains 9:21, Apocalypse 18:12; pl., 2 Timothée 2:20, Apocalypse 2:27; τὰ σ. τῆς λειτουργίας, Hébreux 9:21; pl., τὰ σ., utensils, goods, Matthieu 12:29, Marc 3:27, Luc 17:31; id. of the tackle or gear of a ship (Xen., Polyb., al.); so in sing., τὸ σ., Actes 27:17. Metaphorical, of persons: σ. ἐκλογῆς, Actes 9:15; ὀργῆς, Romains 9:22; ἐλέους, Romains 9:23; σ. εἰς τιμήν (cf. Romains 9:21), 2 Timothée 2:21; of woman, ἀσθενέστερον σ., 1 Pierre 3:7; so perh. τ. ἑαυτοῦ σ., 1 Thessaloniciens 4:4 (but see infr.); of the body, 2 Corinthiens 4:7; so perh. 1 Thessaloniciens 4:4 (but see supr., and see: κτάομαι).†
κτάομαι, -ῶμαι 
[in LXX chiefly for קָנָה ;] 
in pres., impf., fut. and aor., to procure for oneself, get, gain, acquire (the pf. and plpf., to have acquired, hence to possess, do not occur in NT): with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 10:9, Luc 18:12, Actes 8:20; with genitive pret., Actes 22:28; ἐκ with genitive pret., Actes 1:18; τ,ψυχὰς ὑμῶν (MM, xvi), Luc 21:19; τ. ἑαυτοῦ σκεῦος κτᾶσθαι, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:4 (where if σ. = body, κ. must = pf., κέκτημαι; see MM, xvi; M, Th., in l; Field, Notes, 72 f. But σ. is most frequently taken as = wife; see Thayer, see word; Lft., Notes, 53 ff.; ICC, in l).†

G4633.def:
σκηνή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל, also for מִשְׁכָּן, סֻכָּה, etc. ;] 
a tent, booth, tabernacle: Matthieu 17:4, Marc 9:5, Luc 9:33, Hébreux 11:9; αἱ αἰώνιοι σ., Luc 16:9; of the Mosaic tabernacle, Hébreux 8:5 9:2-3, 6 9:8, 21; σ. τ. μαρτυρίου, Actes 7:44; of its heavenly prototype, Hébreux 8:2 9:11, Apocalypse 13:6 15:5 21:3; of the temple, Hébreux 13:10; ἡ σ. τοῦ Μολόχ, Actes 7:43 (LXX); metaphorically, ἡ σ. Δαυείδ Actes 15:16 (LXX).†

G4634.def:
σκηνοπηγία, -ας, ἡ
(σκηνή, πήγνυηι), [in LXX for סֻכָּה, Deutéronome 16:16 31:10, Zacharie 14:16, 18-19; I Esther 5:51, 1Ma.10:21, 2Ma.1:9 2Mac 1:18 * ;] 
prop., the setting up of tents or dwellings (Arist.); in LXX and NT, ἡ σ., ἡ ἑορτή τῆς σ. (called also ἑορτὴ σκηνῶν, Lévitique 23:34, al.; see Deiss., LAE, 116 f.), the feast of Tabernacles: Jean 7:2.†

G4635.def:
σκηνοποιός, -όν
(σκηνή, ποιέω), 
making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: Actes 18:3.†

G4636.def:
σκῆνος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX: Wis.9:15 * ;] 
= σκηνή, 
a tent, tabernacle (C.1., 3071). Metaphorical, of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: 2 Corinthiens 5:1 5:4.†

G4637.def:
σκηνόω, -ῶ
(σκηνή), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַן ;] 
to have one's tabernacle, to dwell (in π. of temporary dwelling, see MM, Exp., xxii): before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Apocalypse 7:15; before ἐν, with dative of person(s), Jean 1:14; id. with dative loc., Apocalypse 12:12 13:6; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Apocalypse 21:3 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκηνόω).†

G4638.def:
σκήνωμα, -τος, τό
(σκηνόω), [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל ;] 
a tent, tabernacle (cf. σκηνή, σκῆνος): of the temple as God's dwelling (Psaumes 132:5, al.), Actes 7:46. Metaphorical, of the body: 2 Pierre 1:13-14.†

G4639.def:
σκιά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for צֵל, 4Ki.20:9 ff., Psaumes 57:1, al.; but σ. and σ. θανάτου are also used for צַלְמָוֶת, Job 3:5, Psaumes 3:4, Ésaïe 9:2 (1) (see ICC, in l), al. ;] 
__1. shadow, shade, caused by interception of light: Marc 4:32, Actes 5:15; metaphorically, σ. θανάτου, of ignorance and error, Matthieu 4:16, Luc 1:79" (LXX) . 
__2. a shadow, the image or outline cast by an object: figuratively, ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σ., Hébreux 8:5; opposite to σῶμα, Colossiens 2:17; opposite to εἰκών, Hébreux 10:1.†

G4640.def:
σκιρτάω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Genèse 25:22 (רָצַץ hithpo.), Psaumes 114:4, 6 (רָקַד), etc. ;] 
to leap: Luc 1:41, 44 6:23.†

G4641.def:
σκληρο-καρδία, -ας, ἡ
(σκληρός, καρδία), [in LXX: Deutéronome 10:16, Jérémie 4:4 (לֵבָב עׇרְלָה), Sir.16:10 (cf. καρδία σκληρά, Sir.3:26-27) * ;] 
hardness of heart: Matthieu 19:8, Marc 10:5 16:14.†

G4643.def:
σκληρότης, -ητος, ἡ
(σκληρός), [in LXX: Deutéronome 9:27 (קְשִׁי), etc. ;] 
hardness; metaphorically, of stubbornness: Romains 2:5.†

G4644.def:
σκληρο-τράχηλος, -ον
(σκληρός, τράχηλος), [in LXX: Exode 33:3, 5 (עֹרֶף ־קָשֶׁה), etc. ;] 
stiff-necked: metaphorically, Actes 7:51.†

G4645.def:
σκληρύνω
(σκληρός), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה hi., also for חָזַק ;] 
to harden. Metaphorical, to harden, make stubborn: with accusative of person(s), Romains 9:18; T. καρδίας (Psaumes 95:8), Hébreux 3:8, 15 4:7. Pass., to become hardened: Actes 19:9, Hébreux 3:13.†

G4646.def:
σκολιός, -ά, -όν 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 32:5 (עִקֵּשׁ), Proverbes 28:18 (σ. ὁδοῖς πορεύεσθαι, for: דֶּרֶךְ עָקַשׁ), Ésaïe 40:4 (עָקֹב), etc. ;] 
curved, bent, winding (opposite to ὀρθός, εὐθύς): Luc 3:5 (LXX). Metaphorical, crooked, perverse, unjust: Actes 2:40, Philippiens 2:15, 1 Pierre 2:18.†

G4647.def:
σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ 
[in LXX: Nombres 33:55 (שֵׂךְ), Osée 2:6 (8) (סִיר), Eze.28:24 (סִלּוֹן), Sir.43:19 * ;] 
anything pointed, esp. 
__1. in cl., a stake 
__2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. with): σ. τῇ σαρκί, 2 Corinthiens 12:7 (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).†

G4648.def:
ακοπέω, -ῶ
(σκοπός), [in LXX: Esther 8:13, 2Ma.4:5 * ;] 
to look at, behold, watch, contemplate. Metaphorical, to look to, consider: with accusative of thing(s), 2 Corinthiens 4:13, Philippiens 2:4; with accusative of person(s), Romains 16:17, Philippiens 3:17; before μή, Luc 11:35; σεαυτόν, before μή (see M, Pr., 192), Galates 6:1 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκοπέω).†
SYN.: βλέπω, θεωρέω, ὁράω

G4649.def:
σκοπός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for צָפָה ;] 
__1. a watcher, watchman (Eze.3:17, al.). 
__2. a mark on which to fix the eye (Wis.5:12, 21, al.). Metaphorical, of an aim or object: Philippiens 3:14.†

G4650.def:
σκορπίζω 
[in LXX for פּוּץ hi., etc. ;] 
in vernac. and in Ion, and late writers for σκεδάννυμι (see MM, xxiii; Rutherford, NPhr., 295), to scatter: ὁ λύκος, Jean 10:12; ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει, Matthieu 12:30, Luc 11:23; pass., before εἰς, with accusative loc., Jean 16:32; of one who dispenses blessings, 2 Corinthiens 9:9 (LXX) (of. δια-σκορπίζομαι).†

G4651.def:
σκορπίος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for עַקְרָב ;] 
a scorpion: Luc 10:19 11:12, Apocalypse 9:3, 5 9:10 †

G4652.def:
σκοτεινός (WH. -τινός), -ή, -όν
(σκότος), [in LXX chiefly for חֹשֶׁךְ and cogn. forms ;] 
dark: opposite to φωτεινός, Matthieu 6:23, Luc 11:34, 36.†

G4653.def:
σκοτία, -ας, ἡ 
[in LXX: Job 28:3 (אֹפֶל), Michée 3:6 (חָשַׁךְ), Ésaïe 16:3 * ;] 
in late writers = σκότος, 
darkness: Jean 6:17 20:1. Metaphorical, 
__(a) of secrecy (opposite to ἐν τ. φωτί): Matthieu 10:27, Luc 12:3; 
__(b) of spiritual darkness: Matthieu 4:16, Jean 1:5 8:12 12:35, 40, 1 Jean 1:5 Jn 2:8-9 Jn 2:11.†

G4654.def:
σκοτίζω
(σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ ;] 
to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, Matthieu 24:29, Marc 13:24, Luc 23:45 (Rec., WH, mg.), Apocalypse 8:12. Metaphorical, of the mind, Romains 1:21 11:10" (LXX) (cf. σκοτόω).†

G4655.def:
σκότος, -ου, ὁ the more usual cl. form (cf.σ., τό), 
darkness: Hébreux 12:18, Rec.†

G4656.def:
σκοτόω, -ῶ
(σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ, קָדַר, שָׁחַר ;] 
to darken: Apocalypse 9:2 16:10. Metaphorical, of the mind! pass., Éphésiens 4:18 (cf. σκοτίζω).†

G4657.def:
σκύβαλον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX: Sir.27:4 * ;] 
refuse, esp. dung (see MM, ii, iii, xxiii): Philippiens 3:8.†

G4658.def:
Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ 
Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: Colossiens 3:11.†

G4659.def:
σκυθρωπός, -όν (also -ή, -όν) 
(σκυθρός, sullen, + ὤψ), [in LXX: Genèse 40:7 (רַע), etc. ;] 
of a gloomy countenance: Matthieu 6:16, Luc 24:17.†

G4660.def:
σκύλλω 
__1. in cl., to skin, flay, rend (Æsch., Anthol.). 
__2. In Hellenistic writers, to vex, trouble, annoy: with accusative of person(s), Marc 5:35, Luc 8:49; pass., ἐσκυλμένοι, distressed, Matthieu 9:36; mid., to trouble oneself, μὴ σκύλλου, Luc 7:6 (frequently in π.; see MM, i, ii, and cf. M, Pr., 89; Abbott, Essays, 87; Kennedy, Sources, 82).†

G4661.def:
σκῦλον
(Rec. σκύλον), -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלָל ;] 
mostly in pl., σκίλα, arms stripped from a foe, spoils: Luc 11:22.†

G4662.def:
σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον
(σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω), 
eaten of worms: Actes 12:23 (cf. 2Ma.9:9, and see MM, xxiii) †

G4663.def:
σκώληξ, -ηκος, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלָע and cogn. forms ;] 
a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaphorically, of fut. punishment, Marc 9:48 (LXX, Ésaïe 66:24; cf. Sir.7:17, Jdth.16:17).†

G4664.def:
σμαράγδινος
(σμάραγδος, which see), 
__1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11). 
__2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Apocalypse 4:3 (for the construction, see Swete, in l; Zorell, see word).†

G4665.def:
σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ
(and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Exode 28:9 (שֹׁהַם) Exode 36:17 (Exode 39:10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Eze.28:13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;] 
emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, see word; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Apocalypse 21:19.†

G4666.def:
σμύρνα
(in some MSS, ζμ-; see Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for מֹר ;] 
myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: Matthieu 2:11, Jean 19:39.†

G4667.def:
Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ 
Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Apocalypse 1:11 2:8.†
Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, 
Apocalypse 1:11 2:8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).†

G4669.def:
σμυρνίζω
(σιύρνα), 
__1. intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79). 
__2. Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., Marc 15:23.†

G4670.def:
Σόδομα, -ων, τά (Heb. סְדֹם), 
Sodom (Genèse 13:10, 12, al.): Matthieu 10:15 11:23-24 Luc 10:12 17:29, Romains 9:29" (LXX), 2 Pierre 2:6, Ju 7, Apocalypse 11:8.†

G4672G.def:
Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Actes 3:11 5:12; in Actes 7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), 
Solomon: Matthieu 1:6-7 6:29 12:42, Luc 11:31 12:27, Jean 10:23, Actes 3:11 5:12 7:47.†

G4672H.def:
Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Actes 3:11 5:12; in Actes 7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), 
Solomon: Matthieu 1:6-7 6:29 12:42, Luc 11:31 12:27, Jean 10:23, Actes 3:11 5:12 7:47.†

G4673.def:
σορός, -οῦ, ἡ 
[in LXX: Genèse 50:26 (אָרוֹן), Job 21:32 A * ;] 
__(a) a cinerary urn (Hom.); 
__(b) a coffin (Hdt., i, 68, 3, a1.): Luc 7:14.†

G4676.def:
σουδάριον, -ου, τό(Lat.), 
handkerchief, kerchief: Luc 19:20, Actes 19:12; used as a head covering for the dead, Jean 11:44 20:7 (cf. Deiss., BS, 223).†

G4677.def:
Σουσάννα, -ης
(cf. Dan LXX TH Su, inscr., 2, 7, al.) 
Susanna: Luc 8:3.†

G4679.def:
σοφίζω
(σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;] 
to make wise, instruct: with accusative of person(s), 2 Timothée 3:15 (cf. Psaumes 19:8 (Psaumes 119:98). As depon., -ομαι; 
__(a) intrans., to become wise (I2Ki.4:27 (3Ki.5:11), Ecclésiaste 2:15, and frequently in Sir.7:5, al.); 
__(b) trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., 2 Pierre 1:16 
(cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).†

G4680.def:
σοφός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;] 
skilled, clever, wise, whether in handicraft, the affairs of life, the sciences or learning: Romains 16:19, 1 Corinthiens 3:10; of the learned, Romains 1:14, 22, 1 Corinthiens 1:19-20 1:26-27 3:18-20; of Jewish teachers, Matthieu 11:25, Luc 10:21; Christian, Matthieu 23:34; of those en­dowed with practical wisdom, 1 Corinthiens 6:5, Éphésiens 5:15, Jacques 3:13; of God, Romains 16:27; compar., τ. μωρὸν τ. θεοῦ σοφώτερον, 1 Corinthiens 1:25.†
SYN.: συνετός, φρόνιμος (see: σοφία, SYN.)

G4681.def:
Σπανία, -ας, ἡ
(= cl. Ἑσπερία or Ἰβηρία; late writers adopted the Roman name, Ἱσπανία (1Ma.8:3) or Σ. as here), 
Spain: Romains 15:24, 28.†

G4682.def:
σπαράσσω 
[in LXX: 2 Rois 22:8 B (גָּעַשׁ hith.), Jean 4:19 (הָמָה) Dan LXX 8:7 (שָׁלַךְ hi.), 3Ma.4:6 * ;] 
__1. to tear, rend, mangle. 
__2. to convulse: Marc 1:26 (see Swete, in l) Marc 9:26, Luc 9:39 
(cf. συν-σπαράσσω).†

G4683.def:
σπαργανόω, -ῶ
(σπάργανον, a swathing-band) [in LXX: Job 38:9, Eze.16:4 (חָתַל pu.)* ;] 
to swathe, wrap in swaddling-clothes: Luc 2:7, 12 (Hipp., Arist., Plut.).†

G4684.def:
σπαταλάω, -ῶ
(σπατάλη, wantonness, luxury, Sir.27:13 *), [in LXX: Eze.16:49 (שָׁקַט hi.), Sir.21:15 * ;] 
to live riotously: 1 Timothée 5:6, Jacques 5:5 (Polyb.).†
SYN.: στρηνιάω, τρυφάω (see Tr., Syn., § liv)

G4685.def:
σπάω 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַף, ;] 
in cl. poët. for ἕλκω; mostly used in mid. (cf. M, Pr., 157), 
to draw: μάχαιραν, Marc 14:47, Actes 16:27,†

G4686.def:
σπείρα, -ης
(on this form of genitive, see M, Pr., 38, 48; Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, 12; Deiss., BS, 186), [in LXX: Jdth.14:11, 2Ma.8:23 2Mac 12:20 2Mac 12:22 * ;] 
__1. (= Lat. spira) anything wound or rolled up, a coil. 
__2. As a military term used (by Polyb. and later writers) of a body of soldiers, a maniple (third part of a cohort) or cohort (see Swete, Mk., 375; Westc., Jo., 251 f.): Matthieu 27:27, Marc 15:16, Jean 18:3, 12, Actes 10:1 21:31 27:1.†

G4687.def:
σπείρω
[in LXX chiefly for זָרַע ;] 
to sow (seed): absol., Matthieu 6:26 13:3-4, 18 25:24, 26, Marc 4:3-4, Luc 8:5 12:24, Jean 4:36, 2 Corinthiens 9:10; with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 13:24, 27 13:37, 39, Marc 4:32, Luc 8:5, 1 Corinthiens 15:36-37; before εἰς, Matthieu 13:22, Marc 4:18; ἐν, Matthieu 13:24, 31; ἐπί, with genitive, Marc 4:31; ἐπί, with accusative, Matthieu 13:20, 23, Marc 4:16, 20; παρά, with accusative, Matthieu 13:19. Metaphorical: 1 Corinthiens 9:11 15:42-44, Galates 6:7-8, Jacques 3:18; in proverbial sayings, Matthieu 25:24, 26, Luc 19:21-22, Jean 4:37, 2 Corinthiens 9:6, Galates 6:7; in interpretation of parables, Matthieu 13:19-23 Marc 4:14-20 †

G4688.def:
σπεκουλάτωρ, -ορος (Rec. -ωρος), ὁ (Lat. speculator), 
__1. prop., a spy or scout. 
__2. An executioner: Marc 6:27 (see Swete, in l).†

G4689.def:
σπένδω 
[in LXX chiefly for נָסַךְ hi. ;] 
to pour out as a drink-offering, make a libation; pass., figuratively, σπένδομαι, I am poured out or offered as a libation (in the shedding of my life-blood): Philippiens 2:17 (see Lft., in l), 2 Timothée 4:6 (for exx. from π., see Milligan, Selections, 114 f.; MM, xxiii).†

G4693.def:
σπήλαιον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for מְעָרָה ;] 
a cave, cavern: Jean 11:38, Hébreux 11:38, Hébreux 6:15; σ. (EV, den) λῃστῶν (Jean 7:11), Matthieu 21:13, Marc 11:17, Luc 19:46.†

G4694.def:
σπιλάς, -άδος, ἡ
(on the gender in Ju, l.with, see Mayor, Ju., 41), 
__1. poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaphorical, of men whose conduct causes danger to others, Ju 12, R, txt. (but see infr.). 
__2. In late writers = σπίλος (which see), a spot, stain; metaphorically, Ju, l.with, R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but see supr.).†

G4695.def:
σπιλόω 
[in LXX: Wis.15:4 * ;] 
to stain, spot, defile: with accusative, Jacques 3:6, Ju 23.†

G4696.def:
σπίλος (Rec. σπῖλος), -ου, ὁ 
__1. a rock, cliff (Arist., al.). 
__2. In late writers = Att.. κηλίς (see Rutherford, NPhr., 87 f.), a spot, stain; metaphorically, 
__(a) of moral blemish: Éphésiens 5:27 
__(b) of riotous and lascivious persons (cf. Dion. Hal., quoted by Mayor, in l): 2 Pierre 2:13.†

G4697.def:
σπλαγχνίζομαι
(σπλάγχνον), [in LXX (act., -ίζω): Proverbes 17:5 A, 2Ma.6:8 (= -εύω) * ;] 
to be moved as to the σπλάγχνα (which see), hence, to feel pity or compassion: absol., Luc 10:33 15:20; ptcp., σπλαγχνισθείς, with indic., Matthieu 18:27 20:34, Marc 1:41; before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), Matthieu 14:14, Luc 7:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Matthieu 15:32, Marc 6:34 8:2 9:22; ωερί, Matthieu 9:36. (The word is elsewhere found only in Sm: 1 Rois 23:21, Eze.24:21, Test. Zeb., 4:6-7; see Thayer, see word; MM, xxiii quote Thumb, Hellen., 123 as practically confirming Lft. on Philippiens 1:8, in the suggestion that the verb was a coinage of the Jewish dispersion.) †

G4698.def:
σπλάγχνον, -ου, τό mostly (in NT always) in pl., σπλάγχνα, -ων, τά, 
[in LXX: Proverbes 12:10 (רַחַם, elsewhere rendered by οἰκτιρμοί, Psaumes 25:6 40:12 and by ἔλεος, Ésaïe 47:6), Proverbes 26:22 (בֶּטֶן), Wis.10:5, Sir.30:7, 2Ma.9:5 (6), al. ;] 
the inward parts (heart, liver, lungs, etc.; Lat. viscera): Actes 1:18. Metaphorical, of the seat of the feelings and of the feelings themselves (in Gk. poets, of anger, anxiety, etc.), the heart, affections (the characteristic LXX and NT reference of the word to feelings of kindness, benevolence and pity, is found in π.; see MM, xxiii; cf. Lft. on Philippiens 1:8): 2 Corinthiens 6:12 7:15, Phm 7 12 20, 1 Jean 3:17; σ. οἰκτιρμοῦ, Colossiens 3:12; σ. καὶ οἰκτιρμοὶ, Philippiens 2:1; σ. ἐλέους θεοῦ; ἡμῶν, Luc 1:78; σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Philippiens 1:8.†

G4699.def:
σπόγγος, -ου, ὁ 
a sponge: Matthieu 27:48, Marc 15:36, Jean 19:29.†
